gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall improvement of GBP 1.922 million on prior year's provisions. This was driven by a GBP 5.890 million improvement on reinsurance acceptances, partially offset by deteriorations of GBP 1.621 million in Marine, Aviation and Transport and GBP 2.094 million in Property. The 2012 year of account, affected by Superstorm Sandy, Oxbow mining, and Canadian floods, showed very little deterioration in the last 12 months, benefiting from re-underwriting efforts. The 2013 year of account was relatively benign, with large losses like the Blue Racer midstream vapour cloud explosion, Julius Klein diamond theft, and EIF Risk Management turbine damage generally falling within reinsurance retentions. Current year (2014) large losses included a turbine fire from EIF Risk Management, generator damage from Eneva, and the MV Sewol capsizing, all of which were below reinsurance attachment points. Prior year events like Superstorm Sandy, Costa Concordia, and Westshore Pipeline also saw increases but remained within reinsurance programs.

The 2013 year of account is relatively benign from a catastrophe, large and attritional loss perspective and the run-off continues to develop as anticipated.

A handful of larger losses were experienced dominated by the Blue Racer midstream vapour cloud explosion, the Julius Klein diamond theft in Cannes and the EIF Risk Management turbine damage mentioned above. All bar the diamond theft fell within the retention of the relevant reinsurance purchased demonstrating the low level impact of these losses.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: The prior-year movement figure is taken from the narrative 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' note which reports an overall improvement of GBP 1,922,000. That note is presented as narrative rather than a full tabular breakdown showing an 'Insurance liabilities' column; the figure has been treated as the gross (insurance liabilities) movement as stated. There is some ambiguity because narrative figures in the Report sometimes refer to net movements after reinsurance; confidence set to 0.8 for the prior-year movement. All monetary amounts were converted from GBP '000 to millions. Named-event years were inferred from the narrative where explicit years were not always repeated.
